Explaining the Freelance Visa in the UAE

The self-employed visa is a residence visa in the United Arab Emirates that allows individuals to remain in the country without a sponsoring company. This provides independence and freedom through a form of self-employment.

This visa includes an independent work permit for the self-employed, which is issued by various licensing authorities located mainly in the free zones of the UAE. Self-employed people can obtain permits and visas through free zones in most emirates.

Licenses and visas can be issued in Dubai in free zones such as Dubai Media City, Dubai Internet City and Dubai Knowledge Park. The self-employed visa is equivalent to a regular residence visa for the UAE (stamped in pink in your passport) and is valid for two or three years.

In Dubai and the United Arab Emirates, a self-employment permit is mandatory for anyone who wishes to provide services publicly and receive a fee, even if their spouse does not require a residence or business visa. Obtaining a self-employment permit is optional, but requires you to work legally within the country.
